clue.text: Free competition for plant

parts.note: free means loose, unconfined
strife is struggle, contention or rivalry

explanation.surface: A free contest is being run to win a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosestrife is a tall flowering waterside herb, so it is a kind of garden or wild plant.

clue.text: Award of excellence without more narcotic

indicators.note: without means outside here, so the award goes round the other piece

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
piu is the Italian musical term for more

explanation.surface: An award for excellence is given without anything more to someone on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: PIU is musical Italian; the Order of Merit (OM) is a British honour for outstanding achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a drug made from poppy sap, a classic narcotic.

clue.text: Jew is timid to prevent entry

parts.note: shy means timid
to lock is to bar a door against entry

explanation.surface: A nervous man bolts his door against visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock is the Jewish moneylender in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: That a girl got married is proved

parts.note: she refers to a girl or woman
wed means got married

explanation.surface: Someone claims it is now established that a young woman has married.
explanation.definitionFit: Shewed is an old spelling of showed, meaning demonstrated.

clue.text: Dire list possibly to use still again

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters might be arranged in another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An awful catalogue is drawn up for reusing a distillery.
explanation.definitionFit: To redistil is to distil once more, putting liquid through the apparatus again.

clue.text: Using every effort to make a man climb above everything

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece stands above the second
in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the man's name is reversed

parts.note: Alf is a man's name
tout is French for all, everything

explanation.surface: A man is urged to scale the heights above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' reverses ALF to FLA; 'above' puts it over TOUT, French for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out means at full speed or with maximum exertion.

clue.text: Theme which makes citizen feel important

parts.note: a subject is a citizen of a monarchy
to matter is to count or be of importance

explanation.surface: A topic that makes an ordinary person feel valued.
explanation.definitionFit: Subject matter is the topic dealt with in a book or talk.

clue.text: Marked pages for chief magistrate to read wrongly

definitions.note: the clue gives a noun phrase; the answer describes a book with such pages

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa

indicators.note: something read wrongly is jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has annotated documents for a magistrate who misreads them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eared book has page corners turned down, worn and creased.

clue.text: Short answer in rising dish and left caper on other side

indicators.note: the short answer is placed in the middle of the reversed dish
in a down entry rising means reading upwards, so the dish is reversed

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish
ans is a short form of answer
an antic is a playful caper

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: put a brief reply in a rising dish and leave a prank across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' turns the dish upside down; 'in' then nests the short answer inside it before L and the caper follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Transatlantic means across the Atlantic, on the far side of the ocean.

clue.text: Oneness for a Mitford girl

explanation.surface: Someone finds wholeness in one of the famous Mitford sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is the state of being one; Unity Mitford was one of the six famous aristocratic Mitford sisters of 1930s Britain.

clue.text: Attempt to get over a dune — shifting

indicators.note: sand that is shifting moves about, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to climb over a sand dune that keeps sliding underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges OVER, A and DUNE, nine letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an earnest try or effort, a synonym of attempt as a noun.

clue.text: Novelist has a tedious person for frolics

indicators.note: the novelist has, that is holds, the other piece inside his name

parts.note: Henry James was an American-born novelist
a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: A writer keeps company with a dull acquaintance on his merry outings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' tells you the novelist's surname holds the dull person; Henry James is the usual crossword novelist of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamborees are lively celebrations or sprees, much like frolics or merrymaking.

clue.text: Poem on the theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem is written about the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a classical building for musical performances, and the name of a British cinema chain, so a playhouse or auditorium.

clue.text: People with crazy ideas are given a hundred lines

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
ranks are lines of soldiers standing side by side

explanation.surface: Eccentrics are made to write out a hundred lines as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranks are eccentrics obsessed with odd notions.

clue.text: Animal makes insect bolt

parts.note: an ant is an insect
to elope is to run off secretly, to bolt

explanation.surface: An insect is driven to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift hoofed mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Was conscious of the air, being a climber

parts.note: wist is an old past tense of wit, meaning knew or was aware
an aria is an air or song in an opera

explanation.surface: Someone sensed a tune in the air while scaling a rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: WIST is archaic English, knew; 'air' is the musical sense, not the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistaria (wisteria) is a twining vine that grows up walls, so a plant that climbs.

clue.text: Part of ship's timbers is reverse of plump, and feeble

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read backwards, applied to the word for plump

parts.note: fat means plump
frail means feeble

explanation.surface: Some of a vessel's timbers are the opposite of stout and weak.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the rail round a ship's stern.

clue.text: To wed and get back home is relevant

parts.note: to mate is to pair or wed

indicators.note: getting back is going backwards, so the word for home is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lair is an animal's home or den

explanation.surface: Getting married and returning home matters to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Material means pertinent or significant, as in material evidence.

clue.text: System of holding land for cricketing activity over the valley

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a run is the basic scoring activity in cricket
a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: A cricket match is played above a valley floor, describing a landholding scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Rundale was an Irish and Scottish system of land tenure with scattered strips held in common.

clue.text: Manipulate the Spanish composer

parts.note: to hand is to handle or manipulate with the hands
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone is told to work the Spanish musician like a puppet.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: One can often find it with battery

definitions.text: One can often find it with battery

parts.words: One can often find it with battery
parts.note: reads like a hunt for a torch's power cell, but refers to the legal pairing of a crime with battery

explanation.definitionFit: Assault and battery is the paired legal charge for threatened and actual violent attack.

clue.text: Right bits of cricket for a football team

parts.note: overs are sets of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: Proper cricket episodes are swapped for a soccer side.
explanation.definitionFit: Rovers is a common British football club name, as in Blackburn Rovers or Bristol Rovers.

clue.text: Claw which is a pound in weight

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the word for weight

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A claw is said to weigh a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: A and L go inside TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Frenchman's chess piece for amphibian's offspring

parts.note: Frog is a slang (offensive) term for a Frenchman, here possessive
a pawn is the lowliest chess piece

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's chessman is swapped for a creature's young.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogspawn is the jelly-covered mass of eggs laid by frogs.

clue.text: Turning up, ring taxi on a Bahamas island

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading upwards, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: a ring is the shape of the letter O
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Someone phones for a cab while turning up on a Caribbean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses OCABA, read top to bottom, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaco is an island group in the northern Bahamas.

clue.text: Pleased and confused with seaside walk

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: the printed words, read as PLEASED plus AN (dialect an' for and), the setter's intended fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased yet bewildered on a promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder has a spare D: ESPLANADE uses PLEASED plus A and N only, so 'and' should read 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level promenade, typically along a seafront.

clue.text: Royal is a weight without one comprehending completely

parts.note: real is an old word for royal, as in real tennis

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the weight surrounds the one

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A monarch is weighed without anyone fully understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: TON goes round I to make TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Realisation is full understanding or awareness of a fact.
